name: Powering AI: Data Center Energy for Utilities and Developers
description: Work through a fictional Texas utility/campus diligence case and labeled alternatives: cited intake, honest load forecasts, settings and flexibility evidence, comparable tariffs, bounded procurement profiles and engine records. Five module Decision Labs and a committee simulation practice conditional decisions; planned workload is 16 hours.
fieldOfStudy: AI in Energy, Utilities and Natural Resources

image.caption: Wirewalk Institute of AI badge: Powering AI: Data Center Energy for Utilities and Developers

criteria.narrative:
To earn this certificate a learner must: complete all 17 lessons in 5 modules, play each of the course's 6 Decision Labs to an ending (the lab score does not count); and pass the final exam: 20 questions, 45 minutes, pass mark 80%, at most 3 attempts, with a 24-hour wait after a failed attempt.

The exam is taken online and is not proctored. The holder's identity is not verified; the name is the one on their account. This is a certificate of completion and assessment issued by Wirewalk Institute of AI. It is not an accreditation, academic credit, license, or a certification from any vendor. Details: https://institute.wirewalk.com/certification/#limits

alignment.targetName: Extract a set of large-load request packets into a cited schema, find duplicate campuses filed under different names, convert MVA to MW at a stated power factor, and list deficiencies against the Texas PURA §37.0561 disclosure elements

alignment.targetName: Build and check an internal probability-weighted large-load sensitivity, distinguish its P10/P50/P90 limits from official ERCOT forecast eligibility, and prepare a method note identifying the §25.370 evidence and submission route
